Here is a detailed description of the illustrative figure, based on the provided methodology and caption.

### 1. Overall Layout and Style

The figure is a wide-aspect-ratio (approximately 3.2:1) diagram designed for a full-width placement in an academic paper. It is set against a pure white background and has a clean, professional, and sophisticated aesthetic. The overall structure consists of three distinct, equal-width panels arranged side-by-side in a left-to-right progression, separated by generous whitespace. Each panel illustrates a different verification formulation using a clear, top-to-bottom "Input → Model → Output" flow. A consistent, muted color palette is used to differentiate the three methods.

**General Styling:**
*   **Background:** Pure white.
*   **Fonts:** A serif font (e.g., Times New Roman) is used for primary labels, while a sans-serif font (e.g., Helvetica) is used for smaller annotations and subtitles.
*   **Shapes & Effects:** All core components are represented as rectangles with 8px rounded corners. A subtle drop shadow (2px offset, 10% opacity) is applied to all boxes to give them a slight lift from the background.
*   **Color Palette:** The palette is professional and harmonious, using steel blue for the first panel, burnt orange for the second, and forest green for the third.
*   **Arrows:** Connections are shown with thin, medium-gray arrows that have small, elegant arrowheads.

---

### 2. Panel (a): CLS — Classification

This panel, labeled **(a)** in the top-left corner, illustrates the classification-based approach. It is visually distinguished by a steel blue color scheme.

*   **Header:** At the very top is a header bar with a solid steel blue fill, labeled "**CLS — Classification**". The bar has rounded top corners.
*   **Input:**
    *   A light gray, rounded rectangle with a thin, lighter gray border is at the top of the flow.
    *   It is labeled "**Code + Test**" in bold.
    *   Below the title, a smaller, gray sans-serif subtitle reads "per-test input".
*   **Model:**
    *   A downward-pointing gray arrow connects the Input to the Model box.
    *   The Model box is a white rounded rectangle with a thin steel blue border.
    *   It is centered and contains the text "**LoRA Model**", potentially accompanied by a small, simple brain or gear icon.
*   **Output:**
    *   Another downward gray arrow connects the Model to the Output box.
    *   The Output is a compact, solid steel blue rounded rectangle with white text.
    *   It contains the bolded text "**PASS / FAIL**".
    *   A smaller line of text below in a lighter blue shade reads "1 token".
*   **Annotations:**
    *   Below the entire flow, an italicized gray annotation reads "Per-test granularity".
    *   To the side of the Output box, a small, circular green badge with a white checkmark (✓) is placed, labeled "diagnostic".

---

### 3. Panel (b): CWM — Code World Model

The central panel, labeled **(b)**, describes the Code World Model approach and uses a burnt orange color scheme. Its output stage is visually more complex than the other two panels.

*   **Header:** A burnt orange header bar, styled like the first panel, is labeled "**CWM — Code World Model**".
*   **Input:**
    *   The Input box is styled identically to panel (a) (light gray, rounded rectangle).
    *   It is labeled "**Code + Test**" with the subtitle "per-test input".
*   **Model:**
    *   A downward arrow leads to the Model box.
    *   This is a white rounded rectangle with a thin burnt orange border, containing the label "**LoRA Model**". The vertical position of this box is aligned with the model boxes in the other two panels.
*   **Output (Two-Stage):**
    *   A downward arrow points to a more complex, taller output section.
    *   **Stage 1 (Generation):** The first part is a solid burnt orange rounded rectangle with white text, labeled "**Execution Output**" in bold. Below this, in a lighter orange, it reads "O(L) tokens".
    *   **Stage 2 (Comparison):** A short arrow points horizontally to the right from the generation box to a second box. This comparison box has a light orange background and dark text. It contains the symbol "**≟ Expected**" with a small gray subtitle below it reading "exact match".
*   **Annotations:**
    *   The annotation "Per-test granularity" is placed below the flow in gray italics.
    *   Near the Output, there is a small, circular red badge with a white 'X' (✗), labeled "format collapse at repo level".

---

### 4. Panel (c): TRAJ — Trajectory

The rightmost panel, labeled **(c)**, represents the trajectory-level formulation using a forest green color scheme. Its input is visually larger to signify a greater volume of data.

*   **Header:** A forest green header bar is labeled "**TRAJ — Trajectory**".
*   **Input:**
    *   The Input box is noticeably taller and wider than in the other two panels. It is styled with a light gray fill and rounded corners.
    *   It is labeled "**Full Patch + All Tests**" in bold. A small icon representing a stack of documents is included to visually reinforce the "all tests" concept.
    *   The gray subtitle reads "patch-level input".
*   **Model:**
    *   A downward arrow connects to the Model box.
    *   This is a white rounded rectangle with a thin forest green border, labeled "**LoRA Model**" and vertically aligned with the other model boxes.
*   **Output:**
    *   A final downward arrow points to the Output box.
    *   This is a compact, solid forest green rounded rectangle with white text, visually similar in size to the output in panel (a).
    *   It is labeled "**RESOLVED / UNRESOLVED**" in bold.
    *   Below, a smaller line of text in a lighter green reads "1 token".
*   **Annotations:**
    *   An italicized gray annotation below the flow reads "Patch-level granularity".
